_howto: This file IS the roadmap page (numap.app/roadmap). Add an item by copying one below.
id: lowercase-with-dashes, and PERMANENT. It is the link we send people (numap.app/roadmap#id), so never rename one.
status: one of the keys in `statuses`. Move an item by changing this field; never delete a shipped or declined item.
body: plain text. Blank line = new paragraph. Links as [text](https://...) or [text](/path).
asks: how many people asked for it through feedback. Leave it out for our own ideas.
heard: YYYY-MM it was first reported. shipped: YYYY-MM-DD it went live (required when status is shipped).
kind: bug | feature | data. Order inside known/planned/declined is the order here (put the most important first); shipped sorts itself by date.
The repo is public: never put a name, email or anything else that identifies who sent feedback. test/unit/roadmap.test.js refuses an email address.

known.label: Known issues
known.blurb: Confirmed problems. Until they are fixed, the note on each one says what to do instead.

planned.label: Planned
planned.blurb: Things we intend to build. No dates: we are students, and coursework comes first.

declined.label: Not planned
declined.blurb: Ideas we have decided against, and why.

items.title: Political Science BA: the capstone and the co-op are one choice, not two
items.body:
The [catalog](https://catalog.northeastern.edu/undergraduate/social-sciences-humanities/political-science/political-science-ba/#programrequirementstext) lets you meet this requirement with POLS 4910, 4915, 4918 or 4942, or with a co-op or study abroad. NU Map shows them as two separate requirements, so it asks you for both.

Until this is fixed, either one is enough. We will also check whether other programs have the same problem.

items.title: Import your courses from a degree audit PDF
items.body: Drop in the PDF of your degree audit and NU Map fills in the courses you have already taken, instead of you entering them one by one. Like everything else in NU Map, the file would be read inside your browser and never uploaded anywhere.

items.title: Graduate after Summer A or Summer B
items.body: Right now the planner only lets you finish in a Spring or a Fall. Some students walk in Spring and take one last set of courses in Summer A, and the plan should be able to end there.

items.title: Mark a term as off
items.body: Take a semester or a summer off, for any reason, and have the planner treat it as a break rather than an empty term it should fill.

items.title: How much work a course really is, from students who took it
items.body: Roughly how many hours a week a course took and how hard it felt, pooled from other students and shown only as anonymous totals. The [privacy policy](/privacy.html) already spells out how it will work, so you can read the terms before it exists.

items.title: Compare courses side by side
items.body: Put two or three courses next to each other: prerequisites, when they run, how full they get and who teaches them.

items.title: Choose the instructor you are planning to take
items.body: Note which professor you intend to take a course with in a given term, using the instructor history NU Map already shows.

items.title: Choose your catalog year, per program
items.body: Your requirements follow the catalog year you entered under, and you can pick a different year for each major or minor.

items.title: Registration restrictions on every course
items.body: Gates like "juniors and seniors only" or "majors only" now come straight from Banner, and the planner checks your class standing against them.

items.title: Courses that left the catalog stay in your plan
items.body: If your catalog year still requires a course Northeastern no longer lists, it stays in NU Map, marked as retired, instead of disappearing from your plan.

items.title: The 50% limit on sharing courses between a major and a minor
items.body: Courses that count toward both your major and your minor are marked, and the minor warns you when it goes over the catalog's limit.

items.title: The eight CPS undergraduate minors
items.body: Minors offered through the College of Professional Studies are now in the program picker.

items.title: Search every course, program and professor from one box
items.body: One search box on every [/data](/data) page.

items.title: Requirements the catalog states in words, not tables
items.body: When a requirement is written as a sentence, NU Map quotes the catalog word for word instead of leaving it out.

items.title: Co-ops and internships register their course
items.body: A co-op or internship term carries the course your program names for it, and you can take one class alongside a full-time co-op.

items.title: Get back a plan you deleted
items.body: Deleted plans go to a trash you can browse and restore from, even after a reload.

items.title: Start from your department's sample plan
items.body: For the 385 programs that publish a Sample Plan of Study, you can preview it and load it into your plan.

items.title: Folders, export and import for your plans
items.body: Organize plans into folders, and export or import them as ordinary files.

items.title: Send a plan with a short code
items.body: Share a plan to another device or a friend with a short code or a QR. It is encrypted before it leaves your browser.

items.title: Course substitutions
items.body: Record a substitution your advisor approved, and the requirements count it.

items.title: Optional grades and GPA
items.body: Enter grades only if you want to. They check minimum-grade requirements and show a GPA, stay in your browser, and are left out of anything you share.

items.title: Links to RateMyHusky
items.body: Courses and professors link to their RateMyHusky pages.

items.title: Plan stats
items.body: See your plan's credit load, departments and pacing at a glance.

items.title: Courses you can take more than once
items.body: Courses the catalog lets you repeat can be placed more than once, up to the catalog's limit.

items.title: Who taught a course, semester by semester
items.body: Three years of instructor history for every course, split by Fall, Spring and summer.

items.title: Registering for classes from NU Map
items.body: Banner is where registration happens, and it has the live seat counts. NU Map is for planning the semesters ahead; plan here, then register on Banner.

items.title: Replacing the official degree audit
items.body: The degree audit is the official record of what you have completed, and your advisor can see approvals that no outside tool can. NU Map checks your plan against the published catalog so you can plan ahead, but always confirm with the audit and your advisor.
